practiceQuestions.q: What is the most common animal represented on Harappan seals?
practiceQuestions.sol: The one-horned mythical creature (unicorn) is by far the most frequent motif on Indus Valley seals.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following materials was NOT used to make Harappan seals?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Harappan civilization was a Bronze Age society and had no knowledge of iron.

practiceQuestions.q: In which direction is the script on Harappan seals generally written?
practiceQuestions.sol: The script is generally written from right to left, though multi-line texts sometimes use the boustrophedon style.

practiceQuestions.q: The deity depicted on the famous 'Pashupati Seal' wears a headgear with how many horns?
practiceQuestions.sol: The deity wears a distinctive three-horned (trisula-like) headdress.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following animals is depicted on the LEFT side of the deity in the Pashupati Seal?
practiceQuestions.sol: The elephant and tiger are on the deity's right side, while the rhinoceros and buffalo are on the left.

practiceQuestions.q: Where were the deer or antelopes depicted on the Pashupati Seal?
opts: On the head of the deity
On the right side of the tiger
practiceQuestions.sol: Two deer or antelopes are depicted directly under the seat/throne of the deity.

practiceQuestions.q: The unicorn depicted on Harappan seals is always shown standing in front of which object?
opts: A cylindrical sacred stand or manger
practiceQuestions.sol: The unicorn is consistently shown facing a two-tiered cylindrical sacred stand, interpreted as a manger or filter.

practiceQuestions.q: Which site yielded a hoard of terracotta sealings showing clear impressions of trade packing materials (mats, cloth)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal's warehouse yielded over 90 terracotta sealings with clear impressions of mats, reeds, and woven fibers on their reverse sides, showing packaging security.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary material of the square Harappan seals?
practiceQuestions.sol: Steatite (talc-based soapstone) was the primary material, accounting for more than 90% of all seals found.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the typical shape of a standard Mature Harappan seal?
practiceQuestions.sol: The standard Mature Harappan seal is square, usually measuring 2x2 inches, featuring a pierced boss on the back.

practiceQuestions.q: Cylindrical seals discovered at Mohenjo-daro show close cultural and commercial contacts with which region?
practiceQuestions.sol: Cylindrical seals are diagnostic of Mesopotamian civilizations. Finding them in Harappan cities indicates bilateral trade.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about the undeciphered Indus script is true?
opts: It is an alphabetic script containing 26 signs.
It is logo-syllabic, containing around 400 pictographic signs.
It was carved only on copper plates, never on stone.
It has been proven to be early Sanskrit.
practiceQuestions.sol: The script is logo-syllabic (each symbol represents a word or syllable) with approximately 400 signs, and remains undeciphered.

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Harappans fire steatite seals after carving them?
opts: To melt the copper inside the stone.
To bake the clay slip, whitening the seal and hardening the soft steatite.
To make them float on water during river trade.
To change their shape into circular buttons.
practiceQuestions.sol: Firing the steatite induces a phase transition into enstatite, turning the soft stone into a hard, glossy white material.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Pashupati Seal' represents a figure in a yogic posture. Which posture is it?
practiceQuestions.sol: The figure is seated with heels pressed together directly under the groin, representing the yogic Mulabandhasana.

practiceQuestions.q: Which animal is depicted on the Pashupati Seal on the RIGHT side of the deity?
practiceQuestions.sol: Tiger and Elephant are carved on the right side of the seated figure.

practiceQuestions.q: The Peepal tree leaf is depicted on several seals. What does this suggest?
opts: The Harappans imported Peepal trees from Europe.
Animistic beliefs and the sacred status of certain trees in Harappan religion.
The use of Peepal leaves as paper currency.
Nothing; it was a random decorative border.
practiceQuestions.sol: Depictions of deities inside Peepal trees indicate nature and animistic worship, which persists in modern Indian traditions.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a key feature on the REVERSE side of a square steatite seal?
opts: An identical copy of the front image
A raised perforated boss (loop) for holding or threading
practiceQuestions.sol: The reverse side has a small raised boss (loop) with a horizontal hole drilled through it for handling or wearing.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is NOT an animal motif depicted on Harappan seals?
practiceQuestions.sol: The cow is never depicted on Harappan seals, though the bull is extremely common.

practiceQuestions.q: In which city was the famous 'Pashupati Seal' excavated?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pashupati Seal was discovered at Mohenjo-daro.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about Harappan seal writing direction is correct?
opts: It was always written from left to right.
It was generally written from right to left, but sometimes alternated in direction (boustrophedon).
It was written in circular spirals.
practiceQuestions.sol: The script was written right-to-left, but multi-line texts used boustrophedon (alternating right-to-left and left-to-right).

practiceQuestions.q: What does a 'sealing' refer to in Harappan archaeology?
opts: The clay impression left by a seal on packaging or cargo
The lock of a warehouse door
A protective wax cover on seals
practiceQuestions.sol: A sealing is the impression made by stamping a seal onto soft wet clay, used to secure packages.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Unicorn' on Harappan seals is characterized by which of the following?
opts: A bull-like body with a single forward-pointing horn
A lion-like face with a horn on its nose
practiceQuestions.sol: The Harappan unicorn resembles a bull (uroch) depicted in profile showing only one horn.

practiceQuestions.q: Copper tablets with inscriptions on one side and animal figures on the other have been found primarily at which sites?
practiceQuestions.sol: Copper tablets or plates have been found in large numbers at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa.

practiceQuestions.q: The longest single inscription found on a Harappan seal consists of how many signs?
practiceQuestions.sol: The longest single inscription contains 26 pictographic signs.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Round button-shaped seals have been discovered at Lothal.
2. Button seals show trade links with the Persian Gulf.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Circular button seals (often called 'Persian Gulf seals') found at Lothal prove trade connections.

practiceQuestions.q: Which tree is most commonly associated with deities on Harappan seals?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Peepal tree (Ficus religiosa) is the most sacred tree represented in Harappan seal iconography.

practiceQuestions.q: The three-horned headgear on the Pashupati figure is believed to represent which of the following?
opts: A crown made of pure gold
A religious or tribal insignia representing bull horns
A protective helmet used in battle
practiceQuestions.sol: The three horns represent a horned headgear, indicating a deity associated with animal and fertility symbolism.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the typical thickness of a square Harappan steatite seal?
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappan seals are relatively thin tablets, typically ranging between 0.5 and 1.5 cm in thickness.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following animals depicted on seals was a water animal?
practiceQuestions.sol: Crocodiles or gharials are depicted on several seals, representing riverine fauna.

practiceQuestions.q: Terracotta sealings with cloth impressions on the back were found in large numbers at Lothal. What does this prove?
opts: Wet clay sealings were pressed onto packaged cloth bundles for trade validation.
The Lothal warehouse was destroyed by a flood of mud.
Clay was used as laundry detergent.
practiceQuestions.sol: Cloth impressions prove that wet clay tags were pressed onto packaged goods (like textiles) to secure and identify them.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Mulabandhasana' yogic pose of the Pashupati figure is characterized by which of the following?
opts: Standing on one leg with arms raised
Seated with knees bent outwards and heels pressed together under the pelvis
Sitting cross-legged with head touching the knees
practiceQuestions.sol: Mulabandhasana is a seated yogic posture where the heels are pressed together close to the body, as shown on the Pashupati Seal.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is the primary reason why Harappan seals are called 'glyptic' art?
opts: Because they were made of metal.
Because they feature carved or engraved designs in intaglio (sunken relief).
Because they were painted with colorful slips.
practiceQuestions.sol: Glyptic art refers to carving or engraving on small stones, particularly in intaglio where the design is cut into the surface.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following features on seals represents the 'Auroch'?
practiceQuestions.sol: The humpless bull (often shown with a single horn in profile) is identified as the wild auroch.

practiceQuestions.q: Which site has yielded seals showing a double-headed shipping vessel (boat) with a cabin?
practiceQuestions.sol: A famous seal showing a boat with a central cabin was excavated at Mohenjo-daro (Lothal also has a terracotta model of a ship).

practiceQuestions.q: What material is 'faience', which was occasionally used to make luxury button seals?
opts: A type of natural gemstone like emerald
A glazed, vitreous ceramic material made of compacted quartz sand and soda
A mix of copper and gold
practiceQuestions.sol: Faience is a synthetic material made of crushed quartz sand glazed with silica, soda, and copper to produce a glossy turquoise surface.

practiceQuestions.q: The pictographic script carved on the seals is also found on which of the following?
opts: A wooden signboard discovered at Dholavira
practiceQuestions.sol: Ten large Indus script symbols were found on a wooden board at Dholavira, known as the 'Dholavira Signboard'.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the average number of characters carved on a typical Harappan seal?
practiceQuestions.sol: Most seals contain short texts averaging 5 to 6 signs.

practiceQuestions.q: Which animal depicted on seals has three heads?
opts: A composite mythical beast showing three different animal heads on a single body
No such animal exists in Harappan art
practiceQuestions.sol: Some composite seals depict a mythical beast combining three heads (such as a bull, ibex, and unicorn) on a single body.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was the most common function of Harappan seals?
opts: To serve as currency coins in daily markets
To stamp trade cargo and verify ownership/guild identification
To write long royal decrees and legal codes
practiceQuestions.sol: Seals were stamped onto clay packings of cargo bags to guarantee security and identify the merchant guild.

practiceQuestions.q: The name 'Pashupati' given to the three-horned figure from Mohenjo-daro translates to:
practiceQuestions.sol: Pashupati translates to 'Lord of the Beasts' or 'Lord of Animals', due to the figure being surrounded by wild beasts.

practiceQuestions.q: The Khetri copper mines of Rajasthan supplied copper, but where did Harappans get the steatite to make seals?
opts: Quarried from the Aravalli hills in Rajasthan and Gujarat
practiceQuestions.sol: Steatite was obtained locally from the talc outcrops of the Aravalli range in Rajasthan and northern Gujarat.

practiceQuestions.q: The standard carving technique for seals, where the motif is cut into the stone so that the impression stands out in relief, is called:
practiceQuestions.sol: Intaglio is the carving technique where the design is engraved into the background, leaving a negative mold.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about the 'unicorn' seal motif is correct?
opts: It represents a real animal that went extinct.
It represents a mythical or composite creature, showing a bull-like body in profile with a single horn.
It was a depiction of a rhinoceros with a modified horn.
It was imported from Greek legends.
practiceQuestions.sol: The unicorn is a mythical creature, combining a bull's body with a single, long, curved horn.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following animals is NOT surrounding the central figure in the Pashupati Seal?
practiceQuestions.sol: The lion is absent from the Pashupati Seal and is not a common animal in Harappan art.

practiceQuestions.q: A seal showing a deity grappling with two tigers on either side is reminiscent of which mythological hero from Mesopotamia?
practiceQuestions.sol: The motif of a hero strangling two tigers resembles the Mesopotamian Epic of Gilgamesh, indicating shared mythological motifs.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary significance of the 'Dholavira Signboard' in the study of Indus writing?
opts: It proved the script was alphabetic.
It represents one of the few examples of large-scale public script characters, rather than small seal carvings.
It was written in gold leaf.
It was a menu card for a restaurant.
practiceQuestions.sol: The signboard features 10 large characters (each 37 cm high) made of white gypsum paste, showing public scale writing.

practiceQuestions.q: Fired clay (terracotta) seals are generally cruder than steatite seals. Why?
opts: They were made by elite priests.
They were quick, cheap seals made by common potters for local use.
They were baked in low-temperature fires.
They were made only for children's games.
practiceQuestions.sol: Terracotta seals were common, cheaper alternatives to the high-quality carved steatite seals used by elite merchants.

practiceQuestions.q: The Indus Valley script is considered 'logo-syllabic'. This means that each sign represents:
opts: A single consonant or vowel sound
A word, an idea, or a syllable sound
practiceQuestions.sol: Logo-syllabic scripts combine logograms (symbols representing words/ideas) with syllabic signs (representing sounds).

practiceQuestions.q: The 'manger' or 'sacred stand' placed in front of the unicorn on seals is often interpreted by archaeologists as:
opts: A standard feeding bowl for domestic cattle
A ritual incense burner or a filter for preparing a sacred drink (like Soma)
A measuring vessel for grain tax
practiceQuestions.sol: The stand is interpreted as a ritual incense burner or a sieve/filter for purifying sacred liquids.

practiceQuestions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Pashupati Seal is correct?
1. The deity has a buffalo-horned headgear.
2. The deity is seated in a yogic pose.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The deity wears a horned crown and is seated in the yogic Mulabandhasana pose.
